issues.display_title: Issue #75: Implement Google OAuth2 For User Authentication
issues.main_description_html:
Description

We need to support Google authentication on the backend so that the frontend can provide a reliable "Login with Google" feature.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Set up Google OAuth2 credentials (Client ID & Client Secret) in environment variables.
  • Create an endpoint to initiate the Google login flow.
  • Create a callback endpoint to validate the authorization code/token from Google.
  • The backend must check if the email returned from Google is already registered in the database:
    • If not registered: automatically create and provision a new user account.
    • If registered: log into the existing account.
  • Return a valid Authentication Token (JWT or Session Cookie) to the frontend upon successful authentication.

RESULT

Added POST /v1/auth/google: accepts { "id_token": "…" }, verifies it against Google's tokeninfo endpoint (signature/expiry validated by Google; we check aud == GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID env and that the email is verified), then finds-or-creates the user by email and returns the same session JWT as /v1/auth/login.

Notes:

  • New users are provisioned with EmailVerified=true and an empty password hash — password login stays impossible until they set one (#63 covers that flow).
  • An existing unverified email/password account is marked verified on first Google login (Google has verified the address).
  • Scope note: the "initiate + callback endpoint" AC was superseded — the frontend's NextAuth Google provider initiates the flow and handles the OAuth callback/state, so the backend only needs this one verification endpoint (agreed with FE task gothru-3d-floormap#219).
  • Unit test covers token validation (aud mismatch, unverified email, missing email, Google rejection).

Env required: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID (same client id as the frontend's AUTH_GOOGLE_ID).

Files: src/action/v1/auth/google.go, src/action/v1/auth/google_test.go, src/controllers/v1/auth/google.go, src/routes/v1/auth.go

RESULT 14/07/26

✅ Implementation:: CockroachDB SQL Migration Runner

Summary

Implemented an explicit SQL migration workflow for CockroachDB/PostgreSQL schema changes. The API no longer needs to rely on GORM AutoMigrate for production schema updates.

Files Changed

  • cmd/migrate/main.go
  • cmd/migrate/main_test.go
  • migrations/202607140001_cockroach_users_cleanup.sql
  • Makefile
  • README.md
  • docs/tasks/cockroach_sql_migration_runner.md

Migration Runner

The runner is a small CLI under cmd/migrate.

Command:

go run ./cmd/migrate -- up

Make target:

make migrate

Behavior:

  • Loads .env using godotenv.
  • Requires DB_DRIVER=postgres.
  • Builds a pgx DSN from DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASS, DB_NAME, and DB_SSLMODE.
  • Reads *.sql files from migrations/.
  • Sorts files by filename.
  • Parses only the -- +migrate Up section.
  • Rejects duplicate version prefixes.
  • Creates public.schema_migrations if missing.
  • Skips versions already recorded in schema_migrations.
  • Executes each SQL statement in autocommit mode.
  • Records the migration version only after all statements succeed.

CockroachDB Compatibility

Several review fixes were applied:

  • schema_migrations.version and schema_migrations.name use TEXT, not Cockroach-only STRING.
  • DDL is not wrapped in one explicit transaction, avoiding Cockroach schema-change edge cases.
  • MySQL environments fail early with a clear DB_DRIVER message instead of a confusing pgx connection error.

First SQL Migration

migrations/202607140001_cockroach_users_cleanup.sql handles the existing users schema cleanup:

  • Ensures uni_users_unique_id exists as a unique index.
  • Creates public.users_id_seq.
  • Sets public.users.id default to nextval('public.users_id_seq').
  • Drops the invalid "{“ column from public.users.

Deployment Flow

Recommended production sequence:

git pull
go run ./cmd/migrate -- up
go build -o bin/api ./cmd/api
pm2 restart mapthru

For shared/staging/production databases:

DB_AUTO_MIGRATE=false

Verification

Ran:

go test ./cmd/migrate
go test ./cmd/exportdata

Both passed.

Context

The backend now runs against CockroachDB for the MapThru database. GORM AutoMigrate caused schema drift and noisy startup errors because CockroachDB represents some unique indexes differently from PostgreSQL constraints.

Goal

Move production schema changes to explicit SQL migrations that are run during deploy, while keeping the API runtime focused on application queries.

Requirements

  • Add a CLI migration runner under cmd/migrate.
  • Load database settings from .env / environment variables.
  • Require DB_DRIVER=postgres so MySQL setups fail with a clear message.
  • Read ordered SQL files from migrations/.
  • Apply only the -- +migrate Up section.
  • Record applied versions in public.schema_migrations.
  • Skip migrations that were already applied.
  • Reject duplicate migration version prefixes before running SQL.
  • Use TEXT columns in schema_migrations for PostgreSQL compatibility.
  • Execute migration statements in autocommit mode so CockroachDB DDL is not marked applied inside a failed explicit transaction.
  • Add make migrate as the standard command.
  • Document the migration flow in README.md.

Implemented Changes

  • Created cmd/migrate/main.go for the migration CLI.
  • Added parser and validation tests in cmd/migrate/main_test.go.
  • Added migrations/202607140001_cockroach_users_cleanup.sql.
  • Added make migrate to Makefile.
  • Updated README.md to document SQL migrations and DB_AUTO_MIGRATE=false for shared/staging/production databases.

First Migration

202607140001_cockroach_users_cleanup.sql:

  • Ensures uni_users_unique_id exists as a unique index.
  • Creates users_id_seq.
  • Sets users.id default to nextval('public.users_id_seq').
  • Drops the invalid "{“ users column created by a previous bad schema migration attempt.

Usage

Run migrations before restarting the API during deploy:

make migrate

or:

go run ./cmd/migrate -- up

Verification

  • go test ./cmd/migrate
  • go test ./cmd/exportdata
